items.followUp: Define the ice point and steam point used to calibrate a thermometer.

rubric.why: The lower fixed point is defined by the melting point of ice.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is the temperature of melting pure ice at standard atmospheric pressure (0 °C).

rubric.why: The upper fixed point is defined by the boiling point of water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is the temperature of boiling water at standard atmospheric pressure (100 °C).

modelAnswer: The lower fixed point is the temperature of pure melting ice at standard atmospheric pressure; it is 0 °C.
The upper fixed point is the temperature of boiling water at standard atmospheric pressure; it is 100 °C.

items.followUp: State Newton’s second law and use it to derive the relation between force, mass and acceleration.

rubric.why: Newton’s second law relates force to the rate of change of momentum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that force is proportional to the rate of change of momentum and acts in its direction.

rubric.why: The derivation uses momentum p = mv for constant mass.
rubric.description: Uses momentum to begin the derivation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for applying p = mv and relating change in momentum to mass and change in velocity.

rubric.why: For constant mass, the rate of change of velocity is acceleration, giving the force relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for deriving F = ma (with the proportionality constant taken as 1 in SI).

rubric.why: The SI unit follows from F = ma.
rubric.description: Defines the SI unit of force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining one newton as the force that gives a 1 kg mass an acceleration of 1 m/s², or stating 1 N = 1 kg m/s².

modelAnswer: Newton’s second law states that the force acting on a body is proportional to the rate of change of its momentum and acts in the direction of that force.
For a body of constant mass m, momentum p = mv.
Therefore, F ∝ change in momentum/time = m(v − u)/t = ma.
In SI, the proportionality constant is 1, so F = ma.
One newton (1 N) is the force that produces an acceleration of 1 m/s² in a mass of 1 kg; 1 N = 1 kg m/s².

items.followUp: Define one newton and write its equivalent in SI base units.

rubric.why: A force is described as a push or pull, or as an interaction that can change motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of force.

rubric.why: The newton is the SI unit of force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the newton (N).

modelAnswer: A force is a push or pull that can change or tend to change the state of rest or motion of a body.
The SI unit of force is the newton (N).

items.followUp: Explain the difference between a base unit and a derived unit, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: Base units are independent units for fundamental quantities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that base units are independent or fundamental units.

rubric.why: Derived units are formed from base units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that derived units are obtained by combining base units.

modelAnswer: Base units are independent units of fundamental physical quantities, such as the metre.
Derived units are obtained by combining base units, such as metres per second (m/s) for speed.

items.followUp: Write two differences between mass and weight.

rubric.why: These are valid properties of mass that distinguish it from weight.
rubric.description: Gives one correct difference concerning mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid distinction, such as mass being the amount of matter, a scalar, or remaining constant.

rubric.why: These are valid properties of weight that distinguish it from mass.
rubric.description: Gives the corresponding difference concerning weight.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid distinction, such as weight being gravitational force, a vector, or varying with gravitational field strength.

modelAnswer: Mass is the amount of matter in a body, whereas weight is the gravitational force acting on it.
Mass is a scalar and remains constant, whereas weight is a vector and can vary with gravitational field strength.

items.followUp: What is random motion? Give one example of a particle moving randomly.

rubric.why: Random motion is irregular and has no predictable direction or path.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing motion as irregular or unpredictable in direction or path.

rubric.why: These are examples of particles exhibiting random motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one suitable example, such as pollen grains in water or dust particles in air.

modelAnswer: Random motion is motion in which a particle moves irregularly and unpredictably, changing its direction continuously.
An example is the random motion of pollen grains suspended in water.

items.followUp: Write the SI units of length, mass, time and luminous intensity.

rubric.why: Kelvin and ampere are the SI units of temperature and electric current.
rubric.description: Gives the temperature and current units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving kelvin (K) for temperature and ampere (A) for electric current.

rubric.why: Newton and coulomb are the SI units of force and electric charge.
rubric.description: Gives the force and charge units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving newton (N) for force and coulomb (C) for electric charge.

modelAnswer: The SI unit of temperature is the kelvin (K), and the SI unit of electric current is the ampere (A).
The SI unit of force is the newton (N), and the SI unit of electric charge is the coulomb (C).

items.followUp: What does a plumb line indicate, and how does it work?

rubric.why: A plumb line consists of a string or thread with a weight attached.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a string or thread carrying a suspended weight (plumb bob).

rubric.why: The suspended weight aligns the line with the vertical direction under gravity.
rubric.description: States what the plumb line indicates.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it indicates the vertical direction.

modelAnswer: A plumb line is a string with a small weight, called a plumb bob, attached to its end.
When suspended freely, it indicates the vertical direction because of gravity.
